## Disagreements

- **NOM-25** (L1 safe, L2 tip): Level 2 tips the no-fault gait from about 24 degrees, level 1 from about 27 (both hold at 20). The level-2 controller keeps the commanded centre of pressure within 90% of the foot, a margin the level-1 limit (A3) does not have: with the full foot, level 2 holds 25 and tips at 26. The ankle stays below its torque limit (15.5 of 20 kN m at 25 degrees). Level 2 is the more pessimistic; the slope limit should rest on it.
- **CAT-04-NOBRAKE** (L1 hard-drop, L2 safe): Level 1 scales leg support force linearly with capacity (assumption A4), so 35% capacity cannot hold the body. In level 2 nearly straight legs need little knee torque, so 35% of the knee torque still holds. A4 is pessimistic for straight-legged stance and optimistic for a deep crouch.
- **CAP-16** (L1 tip, L2 safe): A slow leak at 16 degrees with a 0.16 m CoM offset (above the 0.12 m limit, DQ-011) and load holding working. Level 1 loses balance as its centre-of-pressure limit (L cos(slope) x capacity, A3) shrinks and its legs sink 0.2 m (A4), and tips 30 ms after the hold engages. Level 2's ankle (26.5 kN m adopted, DQ-012; 20 kN m also held) gives more centre-of-pressure authority than A3 as capacity falls, and it holds; with the ankle limited to m g L cos(slope) it tips as level 1 does. Ankle torque is sized against CF4 in SZ-01 (HAZ-WLK-002, SYS-016).
- **SF-01/EC-07** (L1 tip, L2 hard-drop): Load holding fails during a slow leak at 18 degrees, so the walker is lost either way; the models differ in which comes first. Level 1 ties leg force and centre-of-pressure authority to the same capacity (A3, A4) and tips. Level 2 tipped with the earlier assumed torques (ankle 20, knee 60 kN m); with the adopted ankle 26.5 kN m or knee 22.5 kN m (DQ-012), either change alone, the ankle outlasts the knees, the legs fold and the cockpit drops at about 2.8 m/s (the HAZ-PIL-002 mechanism, against 4.1 m/s after a burst).
- **SF-01/EC-08** (L1 tip, L2 safe): A slow leak at 16.5 degrees with load holding working; the pilot's protective stop starts at 3.9 s with 49% capacity. Level 1 plants the second foot, crouches and loses balance as its centre-of-pressure limit shrinks (A3), tipping 45 ms after the hold engages. Level 2 does not complete the stop step at that capacity, stays on the stance foot and holds it with the ankle until the hold engages; with the adopted torques it tips only with the ankle at or below about 12 kN m. The case sits on the actuator-capacity boundary (sim/results/sizing-cf4.md).

Notes are AI drafts (I0). A disagreement is a finding about the models: the level that is closer to the real machine is unknown until hardware data exists.
